title: A locally zero section on an affine neighbourhood vanishes after shrinking
statement: Let X be a scheme in universe u+1, i : X.Opens -> X.Etale with i followed by forget equal to X.restrictFunctor, x a point, H a left adjoint to direct image along X.fromSpecStalk x, and F an abelian etale sheaf with coefficients AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}. Use the neighbourhood diagram D and canonical cocone c of [new-local-stalk-sections-comparison-map]. If A is an opposite neighbourhood of x whose underlying open is affine, and s in D(A) satisfies c(A)(s)=0, there exist an opposite neighbourhood W and an arrow f:A->W such that D(f)(s)=0.

proof.text: Let N be the full subcategory of open neighbourhoods of x whose underlying opens are affine. Every neighbourhood contains an affine neighbourhood, so the fully faithful inclusion j:N -> OpenNhds(x) has a smaller object over every neighbourhood. The Mathlib cofilteredness criterion gives IsCofiltered N. Restrict the supplied functor i along j to obtain D:N -> X.Etale.

The equality i followed by forget = X.restrictFunctor gives over-X isomorphisms from the objects D(U) to the canonical open subschemes. These isomorphisms show each D(U) is affine and its structural map is an open immersion. The canonical LocalStalkSections.lift maps form a cone c with point Spec O_X,x, by lift_naturality. Compose its projections with the over-X isomorphisms and cancel the open inclusions to identify them with fromSpecStalkOfMem. Transport the unique-factorization property of fromSpecStalk_limit_affine_neighbourhoods through these isomorphisms to prove IsLimit c.

Whisker the given LocalStalkSections.cocone by j.op. Its legs are definitionally the adjunction-unit maps followed by the terminal-to-base-change sections in affineOpenSections_cocone_isColimit. Apply that continuity theorem to D, c, X.fromSpecStalk x, lift_fac, and the supplied adjunction. This proves that the whiskered cocone B is a colimit.

Regard A as the object a of N using hA. The assumption hs and additivity of the cocone leg give B_a(s)=B_a(0). Mathlib Concrete.isColimit_exists_of_rep_eq produces an object W and arrows f,g:op(a)->W with D.op(F)(f)(s)=D.op(F)(g)(0). The second side is zero because the map is an abelian-group homomorphism. Apply j.op to W and f; unfolding the restricted diagram gives the required neighbourhood, arrow, and vanishing.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 59.51.5, degree zero: instantiate existing affine-open section continuity on the affine neighbourhood system; use the concrete filtered-colimit equality criterion.

lean.statement: theorem localStalkSections_affine_vanishing {X : Scheme.{u + 1}} (i : X.Opens ⥤ X.Etale) (hi : i ⋙ Scheme.Etale.forget X = X.restrictFunctor) (x : X) (H : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} ⥤ Sheaf (Spec (X.presheaf.stalk x)).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (hH : H ⊣ (X.fromSpecStalk x).Etale.sheafPushforwardContinuous AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} X.smallEtaleTopology (Spec (X.presheaf.stalk x)).smallEtaleTopology) (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (A : (OpenNhds x)ᵒᵖ) (hA : IsAffineOpen A.unop.1) (s : (LocalStalkSections.neighbourhoodDiagram i x F).obj A) (hs : (LocalStalkSections.cocone i hi x H hH F).ι.app A s = 0) : ∃ (W : (OpenNhds x)ᵒᵖ) (f : A ⟶ W), (LocalStalkSections.neighbourhoodDiagram i x F).map f s = 0
